abstract: A 16mm motion-picture camera mounted on a helmet has been used to record simultaneously the scene being viewed by the wearer as well as the point of eye fixation on that scene. The technique has been tested as a means of demonstrating search courses in the survey and interpretation of x-ray films. The analysis of the examiner's eye movements during the viewing of cineradiography may have value in trying to understand and explain the increase in depth awareness brought about by object rotation. A closed-circuit television system was used for the distant transmission of radiographic images, the scanning and search of which were remotely controlled by an observer looking at a display monitor.
